
## Theory Questions

1. Assume that you measure the S parameters of two antennas connected to the ports of a VNA. One is a well-characterized calibration antenna, so you know it’s gain, Gcal. You know the distance between the antennas, r, the S-parameters and the frequencies they were measured at Sxx and ω, and the power level you’ve specified for the VNA, P1. Write a formula for the gain of the non-calibration antenna. You may not assume S11 or S22 are zero in this measurement, though they are small.

We can say simply that the power received is how much power goes through the transmitting antenna and is amplified, accounting for the free space path loss (noting that the $S_{xx}$ parameters are squared because this is power and not voltage ):

$$
\begin{align}
\underbrace{ P_{s r c}(1-S_{11}^{2}) }_{ P_{t}  } G_{tx}G_{rx} \left( \frac{\lambda}{4\pi R}   \right)^{2}=P_{r} 
\end{align}
$$
We can rearrange for $G_{rx}$, noting that $P_{r}=P_{src}S_{21}^{2}$


$$
\begin{align}
\frac{P_{t}S_{21}^{2}  }{P_{src}G_{tx}   } \left( \frac{4\pi R}{\lambda} \right)^{2} = G_{rx}    \\
\frac{S_{21}^{2}  }{(1-S_{11}^{2})G_{ c a l}   } \left( \frac{4\pi R}{\lambda} \right)^{2} = G_{rx}   
\end{align}
$$
We can further simplify,
(note that I call $G_{tx}=G_{c al}$ - i have a snippet for $\mathcal{cal}$ and didn't want to fix it a bunch)

$$
\begin{align}
\lambda= \frac{2\pi c}{\omega}
\end{align}
$$

$$
\begin{align}
 G_{rx}=\frac{S_{21}^{2}  }{(1-S_{11}^{2})G_{ c a l}   } \left( \frac{2 R\omega}{ c} \right)^{2}   
\end{align}
$$

3. Find and read the datasheet for the BBHA9120LF Double Ridged Horn antenna, which is the calibration antenna in our chamber. What are the gain and VSWR of the antenna at 2.4GHz? Use these results to find is |S11| of the antenna at that frequency. [http://www.schwarzbeck.de/en/antennas/broadband-horn-antennas/double-ridged-hornantenna/408-bbha-9120-lf-double-ridged-broadband-horn-antenna.html](http://www.schwarzbeck.de/en/antennas/broadband-horn-antennas/double-ridged-hornantenna/408-bbha-9120-lf-double-ridged-broadband-horn-antenna.html)

VSWR appears to be about 1.5 and $2.4 GHz$

Thus,
$$
\begin{align}
\underbrace{ S }_{ VSWR }= \frac{1-\left| \Gamma \right| }{1+\left| \Gamma \right| } \\
S(1+\left| \Gamma \right| )= 1- \left| \Gamma \right| \\
1-S= \Gamma(1+S) \\
\frac{1-S}{1+S} = \Gamma
\end{align}
$$
Therefore,
$$
\begin{align}
\Gamma=S_{11}= \frac{-0.5}{2.5} = -\frac{1}{5} 
\end{align}
$$

4. Read the specifications page for the PWTC 48-8 anechoic chamber below. What are the maximum and minimum frequencies supported by the absorbers used in the chamber? Determine the frequency at which the test turntable leaves the far field of the calibration antenna. You will need to combine the size of the calibration antenna with the usable internal dimensions of the anechoic chamber to find this frequency.


Distance from antenna edge to turntable edge is 1.295 m, 42 in/1.07 m x 35 in/0.89 m chamber cross-section


distance to turntable is 1.3m, and far field is a valid approximation when we have a distance above 
$$
\frac{2D^{2}}{\lambda}
$$
D = 0.142m

If this is greater than $1.3$m, we are in farfield.
$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{2D^{2}}{\lambda} > 1.3m \\
f= \frac{c}{\lambda} \\
c > \frac{2(0.142)^{2}}{1.3m}f
\end{aligned}
$$
This gets us
$$
f < 9.67 GHz
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}

\frac{\lambda}{2}=D \\
\frac{\Delta f}{f}  \simeq 0.03

$$

inner patch: 13.1cm long axis, 10.3cm short axis
outer patch: 13.85cm x 16.5cm

This would give the ideal center frequency
$$
\begin{aligned}

\lambda = 2 D \\
\frac{c}{2D}=f \\ 

\end{aligned}
$$
